contract.sync_assumed: harness group barrier between calls that reuse the temp storage and the output buffers
contract.sync_performed: internal synchronization as declared in the adapter header, measured inside the call
contract.header_contract: two bf16 rows per call in bf16x2 words, eager bitonic top-k with max and min bf16x2, index recovery from the k-th key, MaxK = round_up(k, LW), both unsorted requirements
contract.type_constraints: measured on bf16 keys with int32 indices
contract.nan_behavior: focus-set inputs contain no NaN, see the adapter header

correctness.notes: oracle passed on every measured cell | 92 cells reported unsupported by the adapter's supported(), listed in correctness.unsupported_cells | phase 3 final evaluation, harness 0.10, nodes gb200-nvl4-ts2-99

low_level: Registers 29 to 255 over the 73 distinct kernels behind the card's cells (10 with register spills, a kernel measured in more than one batch counts once), shared memory 528 to 131088 bytes, harness 0.10 on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99.
Adapter statics: input arrangement packed_rows, output indices, temp storage 1 to 1 bytes, 2 rows per group.
Oracle battery (23 cases per cell plus the measurement seeds) passed on every cell that has a number, 92 cells unsupported by the adapter's contract or the device, no cell failed the oracle.
algorithmic: Random input (the one-node matrix on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99): throughput not_guaranteed wins 13 of 38 cells (runner-up in 7), throughput prefer_smaller_index wins 8 of 35 cells (runner-up in 8).
Where it wins on random input (bf16 N 32, bf16 N 128, bf16 N 256, bf16 N 512, bf16 N 4096), the median margin over the runner-up is +10 percent and over the scope's reference control +364 percent.

Largest random-input deficits (distinct cells, worst regime): bf16 N 2048 k 4 +666 percent behind W5_v4 in throughput prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 4096 k 4 +652 percent behind W5_v4 in throughput prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 2048 k 16 +592 percent behind W5_v4 in throughput prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 4096 k 16 +516 percent behind W5_v4 in throughput prefer_smaller_index.
negative: No sorted output by contract (card: sorted_output_support none). Throughput only by design, the two-row-per-lane form has no latency reading.
The GB200 pass measured random input only on one host (gb200-nvl4-ts2-99): the tie_heavy, shuffled-tie and phase 3b order-check findings for this adapter are on its B200 card.
surprises: None beyond what the tables show.
open_questions: A sorted epilogue for the two-row form, if any workload needs sorted output at throughput.

B200 pass (WINNERS_b200.md, random input on umbriel-b200-047, tie_heavy on 068, shuffled ties on 094, phase 3b on 047): the warp and sub-warp winners agree with GB200 on 359 of 376 common cells (365 of 376 when each cell is compared through the adapters both passes measured, as section 16 of the knowledge base does), the differences are named sub-warp lane-count cells, N 128 sub-warp throughput cells and warp ties within 5 percent, and in the block matrices the B1_idx against B1_det2 throughput ties fall either way. On GB200 the k 64 cells at 128 threads run 3 to 15 percent slower than on B200 (hw-researcher, a generation property) and the aarch64 cicc emits branches for the conditional swaps (T20, 3 to 4 percent).
